answer.reason: Egypt is a whole land, so only the two events that fell on it alone are kept: the death of its firstborn and the drowning of its army.

clauses.english: lost all its firstborn when the LORD smote them at midnight
clauses.quote: at midnight the LORD smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt

clauses.english: saw its pursuing army overthrown by the LORD in the midst of the sea
clauses.quote: the LORD overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea

doubts: Egypt appears in a very large number of verses, many only as a place of travel, a trading partner or a figure of speech; most were left out as not specific to the land.
Verses about Joseph's rule, the bondage of Israel, the plagues and the later prophecies against Egypt were deliberately omitted to keep the line to two events.
